scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a flapping/slow peering -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2)
reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss and stable low latency, the router1<->router2
eBGP session is Established with a steady uptime (not resetting), and no route
churn is observed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the peering is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent checks the BGP
session state/uptime on router1 and router2 and runs a sustained ping pc1->pc2,
finds them stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the peering flapping or resetting router1/router2's BGP to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: A thorough four-phase sweep of the simple_bgp topology found no fault matching the reported symptom. Phase A (infra_sweep + l2_snapshot) returned zero flagged devices: no ACL rules, no static-ARP injection, no duplicate MACs, all interfaces UP with baseline-only carrier counters, and no addressing anomalies on either host. Phase B (bgp_snapshot + tc_snapshot) showed both FRR BGP sessions in Established state with standard 180 s hold / 60 s keepalive timers, connections established = 1 / dropped = 0 on both routers, and zero BGP Notifications exchanged; the tc_snapshot found only the default fq_codel qdisc on all six interfaces — no netem delay, no tbf rate-limiter, no injected packet loss. Phase D (pressure_sweep) found no stress tools, no resource exhaustion, and no suspect processes on any device. A direct inspection of the FRR debug log confirmed the BGP session was established once at startup and has exchanged only regular keepalives since then — no session resets, no Notification messages, no withdrawn prefixes. Interface carrier counters on both inter-router and host-facing links are at zero, ruling out any link-flap history. A process scan found no background flap script, hping, iperf, or netem process that could produce periodic drops. End-to-end ping at the time of investigation showed 0% loss in both directions. In summary, no fault mechanism or historical trace consistent with intermittent packet loss exists in this topology at this time; the reported drops are unconfirmed and no corrective action is indicated.
